sentences.text: The Appellant and his family members stated to have filed a criminal Petition in Crl.P.No.13179/2023, under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the said Criminal case filed by the Respondent.

The above Miscellaneous First Appeal (MFA) referred to mediation and in the course of mediation, the parties hereto have agreed to close all the court cases by resolving their disputes on the following terms and conditions:
NC: 2026:KHC:11765 HC-KAR 1.
That the parties hereto confirm that they have been living separately since 21-03-2017 and they could not reconcile themselves until this date.
They further confirm that there is absolutely no chance of reunion amongst them and therefore they have now agreed and decided to get the marriage between them dissolved by a decree of divorce.
2. That the Appellant has agreed to pay a total sum of Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty thousand only) to the Respondent towards her permanent alimony.
The Respondent has agreed to receive the said amount in full and final settlement of her alimony amount.

The Appellant has agreed to pay the said amount by way of Demand Draft bearing No.371546 dated: 03.03.2025 drawn on State Bank of India,
Malleshwaram, Bengaluru and the same has handed over at the time of reporting this settlement before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the next date of hearing.
3. That the Respondent on receipt of the afore said sum o Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Thousand Only), from the Appellant towards her permanent alimony,
she hereby gives up all her right to claim maintenance or any other claims against the Appellant.

She further confirms that thereafter, she absolutely has no claims in whatsoever nature against the NC: 2026:KHC:11765 HC-KAR Appellant, either for the past or present or in future in this regard and she also has no objection to allow the above Appeal by passing a judgment and Decree to dissolve the marriage between her and the Appellant.

4. In the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties and the offence being the one punishable under Section 498-A of IPC, I deem it appropriate to close the proceedings in the light of the Memorandum of Settlement arrived at between the parties in MFA No.7904/2023.
NC: 2026:KHC:11765 HC-KAR 5.
For the aforesaid reasons, the following order is passed:-
ORDER (i) The petition stands disposed in terms of the Memorandum of Settlement arrived at between the parties in MFA No.7904/2023.
(ii) The proceedings in C.C.No.32364/2018 pending on the file of the XXXIX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (39th A.C.M.M.), Bengaluru, are quashed qua the petitioners.
